note: The PoC obtains a live DOMAttr wrapper from a parsed document, giving access to a real libxml attribute node.
The attribute is imported into another document, exercising attribute cloning/import logic and wrapper/node ownership transitions.
The imported attribute is attached into the destination document, forcing the imported node through the DOM ownership path.
The constructor receives attacker-controlled strings from the script when a DOMAttr wrapper is reinitialized.
A new libxml attribute node is allocated from the supplied strings.
The wrapper's previous node pointer is fetched before replacement.
The previous node is freed here; the vulnerability hypothesis is that imported/moved attribute wrappers can leave this pointer stale or otherwise invalid, causing an invalid free.
The wrapper is updated after the free, so the free is the memory-safety sink in this path.
